title: Diagnose and fix the lost state.json entry during a stale-lock takeover
action: Reproduce store_lock_survives_a_pre_seeded_stale_lock_without_wedging_or_double_entry solo with repetition, instrument the takeover in lock.rs to capture the actual interleaving that admits a second lock holder, name the mechanism from that evidence, then fix it. Remove all temporary instrumentation before capping. Two mechanisms are already eliminated in CONTEXT and must not be re-proposed without new evidence.

truths: The mechanism that admits a second lock holder is named and backed by captured evidence, not inferred from reading.
store_lock_survives_a_pre_seeded_stale_lock_without_wedging_or_double_entry passes 40 consecutive SOLO runs with zero failures (pre-fix rate is about 1 in 10, so 20 runs would be too weak).
A stale lock still never wedges the store: takeover keeps working and at least one racer completes.
No temporary instrumentation remains in the shipped diff.
One full-suite run is recorded green, offered as a record and never as the proof.

acceptance: The mechanism is evidenced and stated in the commit body; the stale-lock test passes 40/40 solo and its sibling 20/20; the takeover still prevents wedging; no instrumentation ships.

trace.outcome: Serialized the stale-lock takeover on an O_EXCL claim keyed to the displaced acquisition; the TOCTOU that admitted a second LockGuard is closed
deviations: Full-file verify command is red on a PRE-EXISTING, unrelated failure: one_claimant_wins_the_cell_and_every_loser_is_a_typed_claimed_refusal (cells-claim JSON corruption in .bee/claims/, not the store lock). Measured 17/20 failures on the pristine base and 16/20 with this change, so it is neither caused nor worsened here. Full concurrency suite recorded: 18 passed, 1 failed (that one). Needs its own fix-first cell.
Fix landed in lock.rs only; workers.rs (also in the cell's files) needed no change and is byte-identical to HEAD.

Reservations for both files were already held under this cell and nickname when the worker started, so `reservations reserve` reported a self-conflict; treated as pre-reserved by the orchestrator, not a foreign hold.

The context's fact 1 ("the lost entry is w0, the FIRST racer") is contradicted by the captured run: the lost racer was w5. The lost racer is whichever won the takeover and was clobbered by the plain acquirer that took the rename vacancy. Context fact 2 (well-formed state.json) held.

Context's open question resolved: read_holder DID observe a freshly created, still-empty lock file (holder_after: null on a rename), so the create_new-then-write_all window at lock.rs:198 is reachable in practice via rename_for_takeover's post-rename read - just not via the staleness path.
